title: POST /books is unreachable in the delivered server (routing bug)
evidence: main.go:11 registers listBooksHandler on the exact pattern "/books"; Go's ServeMux routes POST /books to that exact handler, which returns 405 (handlers.go:50). The createBookHandler call lives inside the "/books/" subtree handler behind `if r.URL.Path == "/books"` (main.go:13), a branch that can never fire because the exact "/books" registration suppresses the trailing-slash redirect. Reproduced standalone with go1.26.6: POST /books -> status=405, mux.Handler matched pattern "/books". createBookHandler (handlers.go:15) and createBook persistence (db.go:91) ARE fully implemented and correct, but are only reachable by calling the handler directly (unit tests) or via the separate corrected mux in TestFullServer (main_test.go:265-274). The README documents `curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/books` (README.md), which returns 405 against the delivered server.
suggestion: Dispatch on method inside the exact "/books" handler (POST->createBookHandler, GET->listBooksHandler), as TestFullServer's mux already does; the "/books" r.URL.Path branch in the "/books/" handler is dead code.

title: README run command `go run main.go` omits the other source files
evidence: README.md Setup section says `go run main.go`, but the program spans db.go, handlers.go, models.go; `go run main.go` fails to build. Should be `go run .`.
suggestion: Change the run instruction to `go run .`.
